detail: Subsidiary lists and RSSD IDs were verified against the FDIC BankFind Suite institutions API (fields FED_RSSD, RSSDHCR, NAMEHCR; data index of 23 October 2026), not the FFIEC NIC, because NIC (www.ffiec.gov) serves a Cloudflare CAPTCHA to automated clients. Both draw on Federal Reserve structure data, but NIC itself was not consulted. The FDIC list reflects active institutions at the time of the pull (late October 2026), not exactly 6/30/2026; all 39 banks have 6/30/2026 Call Reports in the CDR file.

For foreign-owned firms the FDIC top holder is the foreign parent (Barclays PLC, Deutsche Bank AG, The Toronto-Dominion Bank, UBS Group AG, Bank of Montreal, HSBC Holdings plc, Royal Bank of Canada). Their US insured banks are attributed to the US (intermediate) holding company named in the brief; the attribution of the smaller banks (RBC Bank (Georgia) N.A., Deutsche Bank Trust Company Delaware, HSBC Trust Company (Delaware) N.A., BMO Harris Central N.A., TD Bank USA N.A.) to the IHC is inferred from the parent, not read from NIC.

FDIC data adds insured subsidiaries the brief did not list, all included in the rollups: Bank of America California N.A.; JPMorgan Chase Bank, Dearborn; Wells Fargo National Bank West and Wells Fargo Bank South Central N.A.; BNY Mellon N.A., The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company N.A. and BNY Mellon Trust of Delaware; Deutsche Bank Trust Company Delaware; TD Bank USA N.A.; BMO Harris Central N.A.; HSBC Trust Company (Delaware) N.A.; RBC Bank (Georgia) N.A. All report zero reciprocal deposits except none; they add deposits to the denominators. DWS USA Corporation has no insured depository subsidiary.

Seven firms publish a Q1-Q2 2026 NSFR disclosure that could not be downloaded by an automated client (JPMorgan Chase, Capital One, Charles Schwab, U.S. Bancorp, American Express: HTTP 403 bot protection on the IR host; Northern Trust and BMO: connection closed without a response). Their NSFR columns are blank. URLs checked are in data/processed/sources.csv. Manual fix: download in a browser to data/raw/nsfr/<slug>_nsfr_2026q2.pdf, set status=found, re-run scripts 04-07.

Fifth Third (Category IV in Q2 2026; Category III from Q3 2026) and Huntington (Category IV) had no NSFR requirement and publish nothing. RBC US Group Holdings LLC appears as Category III in the Federal Reserve's June 2026 listing (Category IV in 2025) but has published no NSFR disclosure; under the rule's transition timing none is expected for Q2 2026. Nothing was estimated for these firms.

BMO Financial Corp. is Category III (85% NSFR), not Category IV; Charles Schwab and TD Group US Holdings run the full 100% NSFR; American Express became Category II during Q2 2026 with an 85% transition factor; RBC US moved to Category III. The brief's labels are kept in the 'category' column and the verified values in data/reference/holding_companies.csv (category_verified).

Schedule RC-O item 9.a (RCONL190, 'Fully consolidated reciprocal brokered deposits') is completed only by institutions that consolidate another insured depository institution; none of the 39 banks report it (12 banks in the whole population do, all zero). It is shown as not applicable, not as zero.

The 6/30/2026 Call Report precedes the FDIC interim final rule of September 1, 2026 (tiered cap up to $30bn) and the ROAD to Housing Act of July 11, 2026; RC-O item 9 amounts reflect the old cap (lesser of $5bn or 20% of liabilities). From the 9/30/2026 report date RC-O items 9 and 9.a are confidential, so this is the last public quarter for the brokered-reciprocal split.

11 of the 24 holding companies with insured banks report zero reciprocal deposits in RC-E Memorandum item 1.g (including JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, State Street, Northern Trust, American Express, Charles Schwab, Barclays US, TD Group US, BMO). These are reported values, not missing data.

Morgan Stanley, HSBC North America and DWS USA publish image-only tables. Figures were OCR'd (five variants voting) and then checked visually against the rendered page images; DWS USA's template omits the retail rows, so its row 7 is nil by construction. HSBC's Q2 2026 ratio is taken from table row 40 (129.3%).

The CDR bulk file is the FFIEC's 'as of 2026-10-15' extract (see data/raw/call_reports/Readme.txt); amendments filed after that date are not reflected. NSFR PDFs were downloaded on 27 October 2026 and their SHA-256 hashes are recorded in data/processed/sources.csv.

Call Report items are in USD thousands as filed; NSFR amounts are in USD millions as published (DWS USA to two decimals). The dashboard shows $bn to two decimals and percentages to two decimals; the spreadsheet carries the full values.
